title: Correcting the assumption in a negative question
summary: A negative information question can assume something that is not true. Miksi sinä et tule? — Minä tulen.
targetSkills: Correcting the assumption in a negative question
objectives: Recognize when a negative question assumes something untrue.
Correct that assumption with a clear affirmative reply.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun.
A weak stem uses the changed consonants shown in the construction steps; the strong stem keeps the corresponding strong consonants.

A negative information question can assume something that is not true. Miksi et tule? (“Why aren't you coming?”) assumes you are not coming. If you are coming, correct that assumption with an affirmative reply instead of inventing a reason.
keyPoints: Read whether the prompt requests a reason, a negative answer or a correction of the assumption.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: State the true affirmative situation clearly: Minä tulen (“I am coming”). Kyllä can emphasize the correction: Tulen kyllä (“I am coming, actually”). Here prompts explicitly request a correction. A mere kyllä or ei does not give a clear correction of the assumed action.
A natural short reply to “Miksi sinä et tule?” is “Tulen kyllä.” (“I am coming, actually.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: The requested correction is affirmative; repeating a negative clause would confirm the false assumption.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: tulen means I come here. Tulla removes -la and adds e to form tule-, then adds -n: tulen.
lukee means reads here. Use the strong stem luke- and lengthen final e: lukee.
syömme means we eat here. Syö- + -mme gives syömme.
puhuvat means speak here. Puhu- + plural third-person -vat gives puhuvat.
olen means I am here. Olla has the I-form olen: ole- + -n. The ending identifies the speaker.
on means is here. Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.
tulemme means we come here. Use tule- and -mme: tulemme.
ovat means are here. Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.
juon means I drink here. Juoda removes -da and adds -n: juo- + -n gives juon.
menee means goes here. Lengthen the final e of mene-: menee.
luemme means we read here. Use weak lue- and -mme: luemme.

steps: Miksi: why; question asking for a reason. Miksi asks for a reason.
sinä: you; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Sinä addresses one person informally.
et: you do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Et is the singular second-person negative verb.
tule: come; main verb after the negative verb. Remove -n from tulen to obtain the negative main-verb form tule; the negative verb carries the person.
Minä: I; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Minä is the singular first-person subject pronoun, used by a speaker about themself.
tulen: I come; verb (the action or state). Tulla removes -la and adds e to form tule-, then adds -n: tulen.

hän: he or she; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Hän refers to one other person without specifying gender.
ei: not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Ei is the singular third-person present negative verb.
lue: read; main verb after the negative verb. Remove -n from luen to obtain negative lue. Keep the weak stem with k absent.
